key_insight: A reinforcement-learning controller enabled autonomous fixed-wing interception of maneuvering targets in real flight.
engineering_relevance: The approach could extend autonomous interception beyond the short-range, low-altitude limits of quadcopters, though deployment cost and reliability remain unquantified.
method: Mapped filtered monocular-vision observations directly to actuator commands with a neural network.
Trained the policy using proximal policy optimization in a custom Python environment.
Compared against two classical guidance controllers in simulation and tested the policy in real flight.
evidence_signal: The policy outperformed classical controllers under most simulated conditions and successfully intercepted maneuvering fixed-wing targets in flight; the abstract provides no trial counts or success rates.
watch_item: Robustness across lighting, weather, sensing failures, and broader flight conditions is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning
